content: This is question about rational functions. I see that they are defined over docs#Polynomial and not docs#MvPolynomial . I am not a mathematician but a computer scientist and here we regularly deal with multivariate rational functions for complexity reasons. Is there are a reason rational functions are only defined over single-variable polynomials? Is it just a historical accident?

Looks like there's previous discussion in #Is there code for X? > `MvRatFunc`? and https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Searching.20for.20a.20theorem.3A.20Degree.20of.20.60K.2Fk.60.20vs.20.60K.28x.29.2Fk.28x.29.60.2E/near/498514899
Will FractionRing(MvPolynomial R) suffice for your purposes?
I think so yes. A masters student working with me would benefit from it.
What I mean is that the student can define it locally as that fraction field.
So I already suggested this to the student, but I thought it might be better to double check this since I am not a mathematician per se.
